_comment: Vendor task_profiles for this device, shipped as the single
/vendor/etc/task_profiles.json.
This file is the stock system/core/libprocessgroup/profiles/task_profiles_30.json
verbatim (both STune* attributes and all eleven of its profiles are kept,
because /dev/stune is still mounted on cgroup v1 and they work), plus the
cpuset v2 migration described below. It is ONE complete file rather than a
small overlay: libprocessgroup reads a single vendor JSON, and
PRODUCT_COPY_FILES copies files rather than concatenating them, so shipping
the stock file and an overlay to the same destination would only leave
whichever landed last.
Why the cpuset part exists: cpuset is attached to the v2 default hierarchy
(see etc/cgroups.json - mounting it on v1 would call rebind_subsystems() and
pull it back out of v2). The stock /system/etc/task_profiles.json applies the
per-state CPU masks with cpuset JoinCgroup actions, but a JoinCgroup naming a
v2 controller is skipped with a warning by
system/core/libprocessgroup/task_profiles.cpp, so those masks were silently
dropped and every app ended up with cpuset.cpus 0-7.
How the masks are applied instead: a CpusetCpus attribute (File "cpus" for
the v1 hierarchy, FileV2 "cpuset.cpus" for v2) plus a SetAttribute action on
the capacity profiles. SetAttribute resolves through
ProfileAttribute::GetPathForTask(), which for a v2 controller uses the task's
own /proc/<tid>/cgroup path, so the write lands on the task's existing
/apps|system/uid_N/pid_M/cpuset.cpus leaf. No cgroup is created, no task is
moved, and the per-UID/PID hierarchy that cgroup.freeze depends on is
untouched.
The masks are the ones the vendor init rc used to write to /dev/cpuset:
background/system-background/restricted 0-3, foreground 0-6, top-app and
camera-daemon 0-7.
Why ProcessCapacityNormal exists and why CPUSET_SP_DEFAULT is redefined: a
task's leaf keeps whatever mask was written last, so without an explicit
reset a task returning from a restricted or background state would stay
pinned to 0-3. AggregateProfiles are replaced wholesale when re-declared,
so CPUSET_SP_DEFAULT is repeated here with its original TimerSlackNormal
member plus ProcessCapacityNormal.
Note on re-declaring a Profile: TaskProfile::MoveTo() assigns
profile->elements_ = std::move(elements_), so a re-declared profile
REPLACES the stock actions rather than adding to them. That is intended
here: the eight capacity profiles are replaced by their SetAttribute
action, which drops the dead v1 cpuset JoinCgroup that v2 ignores anyway
and adds the mask write that actually works. Any profile that carries a
still-working action must therefore re-list that action - which is why
CameraServicePerformance below repeats its schedtune JoinCgroup next to
the new CpusetCpus SetAttribute.
CameraServicePerformance is consumed by
frameworks/av/services/camera/virtualcamera/virtual_camera.hal.rc
("task_profiles CameraServiceCapacity CameraServicePerformance").
MoveTo replaces the action list, so the still-working schedtune
JoinCgroup is re-listed here next to the new CpusetCpus action: v1
schedtune keeps working while v2 cpuset gets the 0-7 mask.
Profiles.Name: CameraServicePerformance

_comment: The profiles below are re-declarations of profiles that live in the
stock /system/etc/task_profiles.json. TaskProfile::MoveTo() replaces
the action list, so each of these is now exactly its CpusetCpus
SetAttribute action. That deliberately drops the stock cpuset
JoinCgroup: under v2 the loader skips it with a warning anyway, so it
never ran, and keeping it would only add log noise.
Profiles.Name: ProcessCapacityLow

_comment: CameraServiceCapacity has live consumers, so it is not a dead
profile: cameraserver (frameworks/av/camera/cameraserver/cameraserver.rc,
"task_profiles CameraServiceCapacity MaxPerformance"), virtual_camera
(frameworks/av/services/camera/virtualcamera/virtual_camera.hal.rc), the
camera provider HALs under hardware/interfaces/camera/provider,
vendor/xiaomi/chopin/.../camerahalserver.rc, and
system/core/init/service_parser.cpp ConvertTaskFileToProfile().
Its stock JoinCgroup targets the dead /dev/cpuset/camera-daemon path, so
it is replaced by the 0-7 CpusetCpus mask the vendor init rc used to
write there. 0-7 equals the inherited default, so this restores the
documented intent rather than narrowing the CPU set.
Profiles.Name: CameraServiceCapacity

_comment: CPUSET_SP_* aggregates are dispatched by name from
system/core/libprocessgroup/sched_policy.cpp set_cpuset_policy(). Only
CPUSET_SP_DEFAULT is redefined here, to add the mask reset; the others
keep their stock membership from /system/etc/task_profiles.json and
pick up the new SetAttribute through ProcessCapacity*/ServiceCapacity*
automatically.
AggregateProfiles.Name: CPUSET_SP_DEFAULT
